question.problem:
A group of students' math test results are normally distributed with a mean of $70$ and a standard deviation of $6.$ Furthermore, their science test results are normally distributed with a mean of $65$ and a standard deviation of $10,$ while their language test results are normally distributed with a mean of $55$ and a standard deviation of $15.$ Find the probability that a randomly selected student's combined score is more than $200.$ You may assume that the scores on each test are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.6915\,$ | $\,0.6950\,$ | $\,0.6985\,$ | $\,0.7019\,$ | $\,0.7054\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7257\,$ | $\,0.7291\,$ | $\,0.7324\,$ | $\,0.7357\,$ | $\,0.7389\,$ |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7580\,$ | $\,0.7611\,$ | $\,0.7642\,$ | $\,0.7673\,$ | $\,0.7704\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7881\,$ | $\,0.7910\,$ | $\,0.7939\,$ | $\,0.7967\,$ | $\,0.7995\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{1}$, ${X}_{2},$ and ${X}_{3}$ denote the student's math, science, and language test results, respectively. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{1}∼N(70,{6}^{2}),\,{X}_{2}∼N(65,{10}^{2}),\,{X}_{3}∼N(55,{15}^{2}).
$$

Let the random variable $Y$ denote the total score of a randomly selected student. So, we have

$$
Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+{X}_{3}.
$$

The random variable $Y$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =(70+65+55) \\  & =190, \\ \text{Var}[Y] & ={6}^{2}+{10}^{2}+{15}^{2} \\  & =36+100+225 \\  & =361.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
Y∼N(190,361).
$$

In order to find $P(Y>200),$ we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>200) & =P(Z>\frac{200-190}{\sqrt{361}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>0.53) \\  & =1-P(Z<0.53) \\  & =1-Φ(0.53)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(0.53)≈0.7019.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>200) & ≈1-Φ(0.53) \\  & ≈1-0.7019 \\  & =0.2981.\end{aligned}
$$
